name: 73-gated-expr-layers
prompt:
Build a small integer expression calculator in this module as three packages that depend on each other in order, plus a command.
1. Package `lexer` in lexer/: `type Token struct { Kind string; Text string }` and `func Tokens(s string) ([]Token, error)`. Kind is one of "num", "op", "lparen", "rparen"; Text is the source text of the token. Numbers are runs of decimal digits, operators are + - * /, parentheses are ( and ), whitespace separates tokens and is dropped, and any other character is an error. Empty input gives no tokens and no error.
2. Package `parser` in parser/, importing lexer: an exported type `Node` (its shape is yours) and `func Parse(toks []lexer.Token) (Node, error)`. * and / bind tighter than + and -, operators of equal precedence associate to the left, parentheses group, and anything malformed — a missing operand, an unclosed or unopened parenthesis, two numbers in a row, trailing input — is an error rather than a panic.
3. Package `eval` in eval/, importing parser: `func Eval(n parser.Node) (int, error)` evaluating with Go integer arithmetic, where division by zero is an error.
4. `main.go` in package main at the module root: `go run . '2*(3+4)'` prints 14 and exits 0; on any error it prints the error to stderr and exits non-zero.
`go vet ./...` must pass. Your work is judged by tests that call all three packages directly, so keep to the names and signatures above.
